result:
`task_run_failed` events and the failure counters now carry the sandbox backend (`modal` or `hogland`), so operators can filter failure alerts by it. I haven't run any tests, per your instructions.

**Cause.** The `task_run_failed` capture in `mark_failed`, the facade PATCH and the workflow-start failure all built their properties from `TaskRun.analytics_properties()`, which had no backend. The `task_run_failed` workflow events also lacked it. The agent-reported failure path (`observe_agent_turn_failed`) and `posthog_tasks_task_run_failed_total` had no backend label either.

**Changes** (all under `products/tasks/backend/`):
- `models.py`: `TaskRun.analytics_properties()` now includes `sandbox_backend`, read from `state["sandbox_backend"]` and defaulting to `"modal"` when unset. Every event built from it gets the property, including `task_run_failed`.
- `temporal/process_task/workflow.py` and `temporal/execute_sandbox/workflow.py`: the `task_run_failed` workflow event now includes `self.context.sandbox_backend`.
- `metrics.py`: `posthog_tasks_task_run_failed_total` and `posthog_tasks_agent_turn_failed_total` gain a `sandbox_backend` label. Values are bounded to `modal`, `hogland`, `unknown` or `other`. `observe_agent_turn_failed` reads the backend from run state the same way as the analytics property.
- `tests/test_task_run_metrics.py`: the agent-turn-failure tests now expect the new label. One case uses a `hogland` run and the other defaults to `modal`.

Adding a label to an existing Prometheus counter creates new series. Any dashboard or alert that matches these two counters with exact label sets will need the new label, or an aggregation over it.
